primary_diagnosis: Hypothyroidism-Induced Gastrointestinal Dysmotility with Peripheral Myxedema
secondary_diagnoses: Chronic Functional Dyspepsia with Abdominal Distension
Non-Pitting Peripheral Edema secondary to Thyroid Dysfunction
clinical_reasoning: Patient with established hypothyroidism on 100 mcg levothyroxine presents with a 1-year history of persistent abdominal bloating, generalized swelling of hands and feet, and chronic constipation. Suboptimally controlled hypothyroidism causes intestinal hypomotility, delayed gastric emptying, and mucopolysaccharide deposition in dermis and connective tissue (myxedema). Re-evaluating thyroid dosage and metabolic status is essential.
recommended_tests: Comprehensive Thyroid Panel (Free T3, Free T4, Ultrasensitive TSH)
Serum Electrolytes, Creatinine, and Liver Function Tests
